But after they noticed my arrival, they carried on with their work as if I were furniture, and for that I cannot find an explanation that leaves malice out. In the case of one individual especially.

Yes, no connection whatsoever. Nothing to do with my need to report to the main house having disappeared into thin air.

The bandits were carrying quantities of grain out of the rice merchant's shop. Walk past all that, arrive at the main house, puff out my chest and announce, 'The bandit problem is solved'? Such a magnificent clown I would become.

en.html:
My foster mother's command I had not forgotten.
But—impossible.

People like that, how to subdue them without killing? Make an agreement, fight on that agreement, win, and then they throw away the agreement. What was I supposed to do after that?

Until they won, they would never admit defeat. Breaking a promise cost them nothing. We had no strength to punish it. Zubaan de di, zubaan badal di. Give their word, change their word. My mistake was treating the first one as though it came with anything attached.

Naturally. Had the balance of power been different, why would the town have become their meal in the first place?

Their fighting strength overwhelmed ours. Until that fact changed, every clever scheme was empty. My grand wagered contest—what a fool I now looked.

Warriors fallen into banditry. And before that, servants of the traitor Rokuhara. On what basis had I decided these people kept more room in their minds for warrior's pride than for the arrogance of power?

...Utter foolishness. Enough pride to keep a promise, that much human decency: had it remained, why live by plundering like starving animals?

I had gone to a thief and said, please sign here, stealing is now forbidden. He had smiled, signed, and stolen the paper also. Such a splendid victory for my intelligence.

From the start I should have understood. The violence supporting them had to be broken by violence. There was no other solution.

So I would kill.
Destroy their core and scatter the rest.

...Not that I believed my foster mother's path wrong. Win without killing: surely that was what the martial way ought to be.

But such an ideal worked only with a proper human being for an opponent. Reason would not reach these animals. Force only. Strong or weak; that was their entire understanding.

No—perhaps with endless effort, even the true martial way might reach them.
But where was the time?

I did not have it.

Hikaru did not have it!

Every moment mattered. There was no spare time for chasing an ideal. So I would disobey my foster mother.

Forgiveness I could not ask.
I had left a letter in my room, severing our relationship.

—Your foolish son, to subdue beasts, must himself become a beast. Do not avenge me.

Few words only. What had to reach her would reach her.

<ruby>養母<rt>はは</rt></ruby>の戒めを忘れたわけではなかった。
　しかし、――無理だ。

　あのような者どもを、殺さずして下す方策など無い。
　約束を結び、その上で勝負し打ち勝ったすえ、約束
を反故にされてしまうのでは、どう仕様があるという
のか。

　彼らは自分が勝つまで負けを認めないだろう。
　そうしても、約束破りのリスクが彼らには何も無い。
違背に対して、こちらは実力をもって制裁を加える事
ができないのだ。

　当たり前である。
　もし<ruby>力関係<rt>パワーバランス</rt></ruby>がそうではなかったなら、そもそもこの
町がいいように食い物にされている理由もない。

　根本的に彼らの武力が町を圧倒しているという事実
がある以上、これを覆さぬ限りはどのような手も虚し
かった。
　賭け仕合など試みた己が、今は酷く愚かしく思える。

　一体何を根拠にして、山賊にまで身を落とした武士
――しかも前身ときたら裏切り者の六波羅だ――が、
力への驕りよりも士としての矜持に精神の領域を広く
与えているなどと思ったのか。

　……余りにも馬鹿馬鹿しい。
　約束を守るだけの誇りが、それだけの人がましさが
残っていたならば、どうして飢獣の如き略奪で生計を
立てようなどと考えるのだ。

　最初から、悟っていて然るべきだった。
　彼らが拠って立つ暴力を、同じく暴力をもって打ち
崩す以外に解決の道はない、と。

　だから斬る。
　山賊どもの中核を潰して追い散らす。

　……養母の示した道も、誤りだとは決して思わない。
　殺さずして勝つ。確かに武とは、本来そうあらねば
ならぬものだろう。

　だが、その理想が通用するのも相手が真っ当な人間
であればこそだ。
　畜生同然の輩に理は通じない。彼らに通じるのは力
の論理のみ。強いか弱いか、それだけだ。

　いや、果てしない努力を費やせば、あるいは正しき
武の理とて通じるのかもしれないが。
　――そんな時間は無い。

　俺には無い。
　
　光には無い！

　一刻を争う今、理想を追っている余裕は無いのだ。
　だから――養母の命に背く。

　許しは乞えない。
　義絶状を認め、自室へ残してきた。

　――愚子、畜生を制するに己もまた畜生たらざるを
得ず。仇討無用。
　
　簡潔な文面に留めたが、伝えるべきは伝わるだろう。

Patriarch"Those people calling you Mother of the Minato family—I should tell them how you conduct yourself. You ordered Kageaki not to kill the enemy?"
Subaru"..."
Patriarch"Foolish woman! Then he can only wait to be killed. Because HE refuses to kill, why should the bandits show the same consideration?"
Subaru"Haan, that is true..."
Patriarch"People like that put away their blades only when we show strength of our own. Deterrence, it is called. They must understand: we too have the power to kill you."
Patriarch"Not words. Not reason. Only force reaches them."
Kageaki"............"
Subaru"So you kill. ...Once you kill, Head, it ends there. Not the fighting. The peace."
Subaru"Kill someone, and someone is killed in revenge. Kill in revenge for that, and another person is killed. After that, the same thing again. Deeper and deeper into the mud..."
Patriarch"So what? Finish killing them all first. We have more people. There is nothing to fear!"
Subaru"Kill, get killed, go on and on like that. ...Suppose peace does return at the end. What meaning does it have?"

Patriarch"...Dreams. Foolish dreams. And for these you would make Kageaki throw his life away."
Subaru"..."
Patriarch"Heartless woman. What mother behaves like this? Only a foster son, no blood of yours, so whatever happens to him is none of your concern. Is that the matter?"

Subaru"As a warrior, I ordered Kageaki not to kill. Naturally it is harsh..."
Patriarch"What?"
Subaru"Write 'stop' and 'spear' together, and you have the character for the martial way. You think such a thing comes easily?"
Subaru"Kageaki has to cut off the enemy's malice, not the enemy's life. One sentence and I have said it. To DO it, how cruelly hard it is... that I do not need you to explain."
Subaru"Kongming defeated the barbarian king Meng Huo seven times and let him go seven times, to make him submit. Kageaki too may have to do that much."
Patriarch"............ Are you in your senses, Subaru?"
Subaru"Sounds like sleep-talk, Head? But without that much, the blade inside the heart will not break. An iron blade you can break in one go. That is not the martial way. Only force."
Subaru"Force only invites the next war. The true martial way alone can end it. Head, that is what you and I have ordered Kageaki to do."
Patriarch"He will certainly die..."
Subaru"Death is part of a warrior's destiny. Kageaki has made himself ready for that..."
Patriarch"...Such splendid words. A model warrior, you are."

Patriarch"But in war everything depends on fortune! He may have the ability and still fail!"
Subaru"I know."

—There is no other way.

To settle things with the bandits...
To save Hikaru...

No other way was there.

...Yes.
Why had I not seen it?

Something burning inside my head, something like a hot stone, seemed suddenly removed. The muddiness cleared. I could think.

What I had lost sight of a few moments before was now right there in my hand.
Kill the bandit leaders. Then what?

Then what, exactly?
Their organization would break down, certainly.

And then?
They would scatter somewhere? No guarantee. That was only my hopeful thinking.

Without anyone to restrain them, why would they not become still more dangerous? Plunder with less thought, less discrimination, far worse than now? Was that not actually more likely?

How to prevent it, then?
...Not just the leaders. Wipe out every bandit?

What nonsense.
Where was that strength in me?

I would die with the work unfinished. So much for responsibility. Behind me, I would leave the town and bandits wanting to destroy each other.

Nothing solved.
Not one person saved.

To solve it—◆

I must not kill.

Leave the chief's life intact.
Take away only her malice.

Easy? No. Almost impossible. Perhaps the Head was right; perhaps it was a foolish dream.

Yet my foster mother had already staked her life on that path. She was not the one walking it, only the one watching. Still, she had staked it.

I was the one who had to walk it, and I had not been ready. My resolve was shallow. Somewhere I had decided the martial path could not be quite so severe.

Now, at last, I would make myself ready.

――それしかない・・・・・・。

　山賊との諍いを収め……
　光を救うには……
　
　それしか、ない。

　……そうだ。
　何故、気づかなかったのか。

　頭の中の何処かで、昂ぶっていたもの――焼けた石
にも似た何かが、ふと取り除かれたかの心地だった。
　脳漿の澱みが晴れ、意識が澄む。

　数瞬前には見失っていた事柄が、今は手に取るよう
にわかった。
　……敵の頭株を殺して、それでどうなる？

　どうなるというのだ。
　確かに、山賊団の統制は失われるだろう。

　しかし、それからどうなる。
　何処かへ逃散する？　……そんな保証はない。それ
は単なる楽観に過ぎない。

　統制がないだけに一段と厄介な集団と化し、今より
も遥かに無思慮にして無差別な略奪を始める事はない
などと、どうして言えようか。
　むしろその方が可能性は高いのではないか。

　かような事態を未然に防ぐには、どう仕様がある。
　……いっそ頭株だけと云わず、山賊団を全滅させて
しまうか。

　馬鹿な。
　そんな力が、俺のどこにあるだろう。

　無責任にも、中途で斃れるに決まっている。
　そして、後には大きな災いを――町と山賊団の間に
絶滅的な敵意を――残す。

　何も解決しない。
　誰一人、救われない。

　解決するには――◆
　
　やはり、殺してはならないのだ。

　山賊の頭目の命を奪わず、
　その悪意だけを奪わねばならない。

　容易くはなかろう。
　いや至難であろう。本家の言う通り、夢物語という
ものかもしれない。

　しかし、養母は既にその道へ一命を賭している。
　自らは動かず、ただ見守る立場でありながら。

　当の俺にこそ、その覚悟が無かった。
　心構えに甘さがあった。どこかで武の道の峻厳なる
を軽く見ていた。

　だが、今こそ心胆はらを据えよう。

The letter disowning myself from the family. That I had forgotten to dispose of.
